findings.claim: The retry attempt kind is derived only from the item's current state being unknown, so an unknown upload whose original-name retry fails before init answers (state becomes failed) is retried next as Attempt.first and takes a (N) suffix.
findings.impact: If the first attempt had actually landed, the second retry's init answers 409 and the file is uploaded again as '<stem> (1).<ext>'. This is a duplicate file with a second inbox row, which I7 says a retry never creates.
findings.evidence: ios/LitloftShare/ShareSendQueue.swift run(): `let attempt: Attempt = statuses[index].state == .unknown ? .again : .first`. In sendFile the init catch returns outcome(for:unanswered:.failed(.genericFailure)) or .stopped(.cannotReach), and run() then sets state .failed, losing the 'may already have landed' knowledge. The next retry or retryItem evaluates state == .failed and uses .first. The new test barRetryUnknownUsesOriginalName covers only unknown to saved in one retry.
findings.repro: Unknown file item after an unanswered /complete. Press retry; the init request times out or returns 5xx, so the item becomes failed. Press retry again with the server healthy: init answers 409 for the original name and the item uploads as 'name (1).ext'. Mutation: a test with that sequence would fail. Not run.

bucket_proposal.reason: I7: a retry never takes a suffix; I6: the retry's init with the original name decides after an unanswered /complete.

findings.proposed_fix: Keep a per-item 'maybeLanded' flag set when an item becomes unknown and cleared only when init succeeds or answers 409. Choose .again from that flag, not from the displayed state.

findings.claim: After the fix, any transport error on /complete, including notConnectedToInternet or cannotConnectToHost, is polled by-path for the whole window, and the local-network-denied or unreachable stop is not applied there.
findings.impact: With the server really gone, the viewer waits at least 2 minutes in 'checking' before the item turns unknown. The queue-stopped state appears only when the next item's init fails.
findings.evidence: ShareSendQueue.swift /complete catch: `catch is ShareAPIError { if cancelling { return .cancelled } }` then pollForFile.

bucket_proposal.reason: I6 favours the by-path check after an unanswered /complete, so no invariant is broken. The delay is a usability cost only.

specification_compliance: I4: the drive picked after a 404/403 now goes through the queue (pickDriveForQueue called from pickDrive when a queue exists), the Retry button is shown whenever a queue exists, and the new driveAfterStop test covers the path. The earlier duplicate-save problem looks fixed.

I6/I7: the attempt kind is now chosen per item in run(), which fixes the queue-level retry for items that are unknown at that moment. A residual gap remains when the item leaves the unknown state first (F1).
I6: transport errors on /complete are polled by-path, as the invariant says.
I5: the added tests cover foreign cookie domains, a viewer without a token, and other port/scheme origins. They look consistent with the code shown.
regression_risks: Moving the attempt choice into run() means every path into run() now reads the item's state. Any new intermediate state between unknown and the retry changes retry semantics silently.
ServerSettings and WebViewModel now require an explicit sharedSession. Any call site missed by the fix commit fails to compile, so the risk is a build break, not a behavior change.
test_coverage: New tests: bar retry of an unknown file keeps the original name; a dropped /complete is polled; driveAfterStop covers drive change, fixed folder and retry; I5 origin tests. None covers unknown, then a failed retry before init answers, then another retry (F1).
Tests inject FakeSharedSession, so runs do not touch the real App Group or keychain.
not_verified: I did not build or run anything, and I did not run the Swift tests.
I did not read ShareViewController, ShareStrings or the test support files beyond the fix diff.
I did not re-check the backend, frontend or the I8-I10 behaviour in this round.
Whether pickDrive during sending is truly blocked in the view (canPickDrive) on a device was not checked.
trajectory: The fix commit (97ce878) removed the `attempt` parameter from run() and the branch in retryItem, and put one per-item decision in run(), so one branch was moved, not added. It removed the isUnreachable branch from the /complete catch, so that is a removal. It added canPickDrive, canPickFolder, hasQueue and savedDestination, and it made pickDrive route to the queue (the dead pickDriveForQueue became private and used). Those are guards on one existing state, not a repeat of earlier rounds' additions. The two other fix commits are docs records. The remaining gap (F1) is the same kind as the r2 F2: retry semantics are inferred from a displayed state, not from a fact about the item. That is a small sign of patching, but it is not yet a repeated addition of branches or states.
